instruction_given_to_self: Read the round-3 disagreement slice (dense vs the round-2 VA_nl; rows read in rounds 1-2 excluded). Propose 15 quality-relevant criteria. Per prereg Amendment 2, proposal SHAPE IS HELD CONSTANT with round 2: interaction-shaped / composite emphasis, same 10-of-15 composite proportion, so the round-2 -> round-3 comparison is apples-to-apples. The belief-change salvage rewrite enters here as a FRESH Track-A proposal (A36), reworded to be merit-bearing rather than genre-neutral -- the round-2 arbiter's objection was that the original instruction explicitly stipulated both sides were legitimate. Label-blind: `judgement` was never loaded; no criterion references acceptance or any outcome.
scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the abstract gives no evidence bearing on the criterion

criteria.name: Efficiency gain stated TOGETHER WITH verified non-degradation
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how concretely the abstract quantifies a reduction in cost (compute, samples, memory, latency, annotation), and separately how explicitly it establishes that quality was NOT lost in exchange; score 0-10 for BOTH together, low when a saving is claimed without a parity check and low when parity is asserted with no quantified saving.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH00 (ESC: sampling reduced by 33.8-84.2% across six named benchmarks 'while attaining comparable performances'), R3-DH27 (ShadowKV: 6x batch, 3.04x throughput 'without sacrificing accuracy'), R3-DH19 (narrows the LoRA/full-fine-tuning gap 'without the GPU memory burden'), R3-DH02. Distinct from round-2 A23 (cost of the method versus its gain): here the cost reduction IS the contribution and the criterion asks whether parity was actually demonstrated.

criteria.name: Reinterpretation TOGETHER WITH the machinery it unlocks
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract re-describes a familiar object as a different kind of object, and separately whether it names the specific new tools, architectures, or algorithms that this re-description makes available; score 0-10 for BOTH, low when a reinterpretation is offered with no consequence and low when new machinery appears without a reinterpretation motivating it.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH05 ('we interpret MLMs as energy-based sequence models', which then licenses a Metropolis-Hastings sampling scheme), R3-DH11 ('views the discriminator as an energy function', which 'allows to use a wide variety of architectures and loss functionals'), R3-DH04 (action abstraction recast as an MDP, then solved with RL+CFR), R3-DH22 (k-hyperplane clustering restated in p-norms to strengthen the branch-and-bound). Round-1 A02 scored reframing alone and round-2 A16 scored subsumption; neither asks what the move BUYS.

criteria.name: Structural property of an existing system identified TOGETHER WITH being exploited
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract identifies a specific structural or behavioural property of an existing method, model, or data regime, and separately whether the proposed work turns that property into leverage; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER. Score low when a property is merely observed and low when a fix arrives with no property behind it.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH02 (soft gates sit in a middle state and overfit; pushing them to 0/1 puts them in flat regions that generalise better), R3-DH26 (locality and symmetry identified as the core function of positional encodings, then used to design a simpler injection), R3-DH12 (an entropy-minimisation pressure detected in emergent languages, then linked to robustness), R3-DH19 (LoRA runs with different seeds have complementary strengths, therefore fuse them).

criteria.name: Limitation-remedy correspondence — each named limitation has its own matched fix
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how specifically the abstract enumerates limitations of prior work, and separately whether each enumerated limitation is answered by a distinct, identifiable remedy; score 0-10 for the one-to-one CORRESPONDENCE, low when limitations are listed but the response is a single undifferentiated system, and low when remedies appear without stated limitations.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH01 names two limitations (program aliasing; unused syntax checkability) and supplies one targeted procedure for each; R3-DH14 names two causes of texture drift and answers each with a specific mechanism; R3-DH23 names two autoregressive drawbacks and unifies atom/bond generation to address both. Contrast R3-DL52, which names stragglers and adversaries and responds with one blended pipeline. Round-1 A13 scored whether contributions are separable; this scores whether they are ANSWERS to stated problems.

criteria.name: Provable guarantee TOGETHER WITH demonstrated practicality
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract states a formal guarantee (a rate, bound, convergence, or optimality result), and separately whether it shows the method is practical to run (efficiency, simplicity, or empirical competitiveness); score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score NA when neither is claimed.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH29 ('the sharpest known regret bound for tabular RL under the mildest assumptions' AND 'a practical and computationally efficient approach', with empirical evaluation), R3-DH20 (sublinear regret plus experiments), R3-DH22 (approximation-factor lower bounds plus 1.5-order-of-magnitude speedups). Contrast R3-DL47 and R3-DL30, which give rates with no practicality evidence. Round-2 A22 scored whether experiments TEST the theory; this scores whether theory and usability are both delivered, which is the pattern the dense-high side shows.

criteria.name: Overturns a stated prior belief — the old belief is named and the evidence against it is given
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract explicitly names a belief, assumption, or expectation that the field currently holds, and separately whether it presents evidence or argument that this belief is wrong or incomplete; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low when a result is merely reported without contact with any prior expectation, and low when a prior belief is invoked but nothing is offered against it.
criteria.rationale: The merit-bearing rewrite of round-2's re-routed 'belief-change' criterion. The round-2 arbiter's objection was that the original instruction stipulated both contribution genres were legitimate, making it a value-neutral genre classifier; this version scores an epistemic act (naming and contradicting a held belief) and has a clear low end. Exemplars: R3-DL37 ('conventional wisdom suggests that single-step learning is not generalizable and should yield poor performance; yet, distillation defies these expectations'), R3-DL54 (noisy raw labels with early stopping beat the clean labelled dataset), R3-DL51 (answers an open question about bias-only universal approximation), R3-DH05 ('it is still an open question if these MLMs specify a principled probability distribution').

criteria.name: Attribution — which component produces the gain, stated TOGETHER WITH the gain
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract reports an improvement with a magnitude, and separately whether it attributes that improvement to an identified part of the method rather than to the system as a whole; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low for a headline number with no attribution and low for a story about mechanism with no magnitude.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH07 (AUGCAL's two named interventions, each tied to a listed effect on calibration), R3-DH26 (the specific simplification is credited with the gain on 10 downstream tasks), R3-DH00 (the early-stopping scheme is what produces each per-benchmark reduction). Contrast R3-DL32 and R3-DL49, where several components are introduced and one aggregate improvement is reported. Round-2 A24 scored whether the evaluation DISCRIMINATES hypotheses; this scores causal attribution of the reported gain.

criteria.name: Currency of the comparison TOGETHER WITH the margin over it
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how current and strong the methods being compared against are (named, recent, credible competitors versus generic or dated baselines), and separately how clearly the margin over them is stated; score 0-10 for BOTH together.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH04 (beats ReBeL and Slumbot, both named strong HUNL agents), R3-DH05 (compared against two specifically cited undirected-generation approaches), R3-DH27 (evaluated across RULER, LongBench, Needle-In-A-Haystack and six named long-context models). Contrast R3-DL43 and R3-DL49, which report gains over 'baseline methods' and 'state-of-the-art' without naming the competitor. Round-1 A03 scored whether a headline number is anchored to a named baseline; this adds whether that baseline is a CURRENT and demanding one.

criteria.name: Claim scope matches method scope
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how broad the abstract's stated contribution is, and separately how broad the method or analysis actually demonstrated is; score 0-10 for the MATCH between them — high when a narrow method is claimed narrowly or a broad method is genuinely shown broadly, low when the claim is wider than what was done.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH24 claims exactly what it shows ('we analyze why and when it manages to do so'); R3-DH12 confines itself to 'the basic two-agent, one-exchange setup'. Contrast R3-DL33, which moves from a dynamical-systems learner to 'hints at how intelligent behavior might emerge', and R3-DL42, whose framework is evaluated on one benchmark suite. Related to round-1 A10 (ambition x evidence specificity) but scores CALIBRATION rather than the specificity of evidence, so a modest well-matched paper scores high here and low on A10.

criteria.name: Negative space — what the method does not do, stated alongside what it does
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract delimits its contribution — the regime it does not cover, the case it does not handle, the question it leaves open — and separately whether it is clear about what it does deliver; score 0-10 for BOTH together. Score low both for an unbounded claim and for a work described only by its boundaries.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH15 ('almost always relying on human priors' delimits prior art, and Ada's scope is bounded to two named benchmarks), R3-DH05 (states explicitly that the masked conditionals alone do NOT yield the target stationary distribution), R3-DH12 (closes by discussing implications rather than claiming them). Round-1 A11 scored whether costs are mentioned at all and was near-inert; delimiting the CONTRIBUTION is a different act from pricing it.

criteria.name: Assumption load TOGETHER WITH the strength of what is concluded from it
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge how many and how restrictive the stated assumptions are, and separately how strong the conclusion drawn under them is; score 0-10 for the RATIO — high when a strong conclusion follows from mild or clearly stated assumptions, low when a strong conclusion rests on heavy or unstated ones.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH29 ('under the mildest assumptions' is the explicit selling point), R3-DL46 ('our results are almost tight if we do not make any assumptions on the inductive bias'), R3-DL51 (fixed random weights, only biases trained — a deliberately austere hypothesis with a universal-approximation conclusion). Round-1 A09 asked whether theory scope is stated at all; this scores the exchange rate between assumptions and conclusions, which is the thing reviewers actually weigh.

criteria.name: Prior failure demonstrated TOGETHER WITH a fix aimed at exactly that failure
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract establishes that existing approaches fail in some concrete way — ideally shown rather than asserted — and separately whether the proposed method is targeted at that specific failure rather than being a general improvement; score 0-10 for the two TOGETHER.
criteria.rationale: R3-DL50 shows that recent inverse-folding methods improve sequence recovery while foldable diversity does NOT increase, then targets diversity specifically; R3-DH07 ties Sim2Real mispredictions to miscalibration and then targets calibration; R3-DH03 identifies that prototype methods either lose generalisation or lack quantitative evaluation, and addresses both. Round-1 A08 scored whether a failure mode is diagnosed; this adds whether the remedy is AIMED at it, which is the coupling the dense-high side shows.

criteria.name: Imported tool TOGETHER WITH justification that the analogy holds
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the work brings in machinery from another field or subfield AND gives a reason the transfer is legitimate (a structural correspondence, a shared formal property), as opposed to applying an external technique because it is available. Score NA when nothing is imported.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH02 (the Gumbel-Softmax trick imported from variational methods, justified by the need for discrete gate values under backpropagation), R3-DH05 (Metropolis-Hastings imported, with a proof about the stationary distribution justifying it), R3-DH17 (conditional transport theory imported into topic modelling), R3-DL39 (information geometry plus generalized additive models). A non-composite criterion, kept because the round-2 evidence pointed to composite/simple COMPLEMENTARITY rather than composite superiority.

criteria.name: Establishes the problem is hard AND that it is nonetheless tractable
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge whether the abstract gives a concrete reason the problem resists solution (a complexity result, a structural obstacle, a documented failure), and separately whether it shows the obstacle can actually be got around; score 0-10 for BOTH together.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH22 (global optimality for k-hyperplane clustering is hard; strengthened formulations yield nonzero lower bounds in linearly rather than exponentially many nodes), R3-DH04 (large state spaces and computational complexity in IIEFGs, answered by a two-phase RL+CFR trade-off), R3-DH20 (preference feedback 'arguably contains less information than the scalar reward, which makes Pref-RMAB seemingly more difficult', then a sublinear-regret algorithm). Round-1 A12 scored whether motivation explains difficulty; the tractability half is new.

criteria.name: Internal consistency — the closing claim matches the opening claim in strength
criteria.instruction: Composite: judge the strength of the contribution promised in the abstract's opening framing, and separately the strength of what is asserted in its closing sentences; score 0-10 for CONSISTENCY between them, low when the abstract escalates at the end beyond what the body of the abstract supports.
criteria.rationale: R3-DH24 opens and closes at the same modest register; R3-DH12 opens on information-theoretic complexity and closes on 'implications ... for the study of natural and artificial communication systems' — a mild escalation. R3-DL33 opens on a learning system for self-organization and closes on 'how intelligent behavior might emerge'; R3-DL34 escalates to 'urgent need'. Distinct from round-2 A18 (restraint), which compared language to RESULTS; this compares the abstract's own opening to its own ending, so it needs no view about the results.

protocol_deviation.what: Prereg Amendment 2 requires proposal SHAPE held constant from round 3 on. Round 2 was 10/15 composite; round 3 was authored 14/15 composite. The file's own n_composite field said 10 and was wrong.
protocol_deviation.detected: post hoc, by counting the per-criterion `composite` flags during the round-3 mechanism analysis (the composite-vs-simple sub-block split returned n=1 for the non-composite arm)
protocol_deviation.consequence: the round-2 -> round-3 comparison is NOT the clean apples-to-apples contrast Amendment 2 intended: round 3 was MORE composite-heavy, not equally so
protocol_deviation.interpretation: this cuts AGAINST the round-2 hypothesis that composite shape drives closure gain -- round 3 had more composites and produced +.0001 versus round 2's +.0095 -- so shape alone does not explain the round-2 gain
protocol_deviation.not_corrected_by: re-authoring, which would be freeze-before-eval violation now that round-3 scores exist; reported instead
